text: The appellant agreed to purchase land and paid Rs 25,000 as earnest money. The vendor forfeited the amount when the sale deed was not executed. The question is whether a party may forfeit money without proving loss. Section 74 of the Contract Act limits recovery to reasonable compensation. Forfeiture beyond reasonable compensation is not permissible. The appeal is partly allowed.

text: The employer withheld gratuity alleging misconduct. Whether gratuity can be forfeited absent proof of loss. Following (1963) 3 SCR 515, actual loss must be shown before forfeiture. The withholding is set aside.
sentences: The employer withheld gratuity alleging misconduct.
Whether gratuity can be forfeited absent proof of loss.
Following (1963) 3 SCR 515, actual loss must be shown before forfeiture.
The withholding is set aside.

text: The buyer defaulted on payment under an agreement to sell. Whether the earnest money clause permits forfeiture of the full deposit. The ratio in (1963) 3 SCR 515 is distinguishable as the deposit here was nominal. The appeal is dismissed.

text: The tenant paid an advance which the landlord retained. Whether retention of advance requires proof of damage. Relying on AIR 1963 SC 1405, the landlord must prove loss. The petition is allowed.
